brief: Goldman's Bobby Molavi argues the index level hides deterioration underneath. The S&P closed last week up 10bps and the Nasdaq up 40bps while oil, yields and fear broke out, leaving the market within 50bps of where it started. A dovish Waller, a hawkish Hammack and a 162k August payrolls print that beat estimates by over 100k with June and July revised up leave a Fed he calls hard to read, with CPI next to set the tone. The AI earnings engine, now led by software rather than semis, has held the index up against oil, inflation, rates and politics, but he says the return profile from here skews negative. Financing is the mechanism: AI capex has shifted from cash to cash, debt and equity, big tech plus SPV issuance is tracking close to $250bn and around 70% of Treasury issuance, and that lands as $10 trillion of debt needs refinancing with China and Japan less engaged. He reads price action as showing Bessent's buyback of over $5bn has not worked. Investors stay long gross with duration and hike protection, rotating defensively.
